statement: This is original synthetic engineering integration code, not an upstream issue or a member of the formal challenge dataset. Repair the CPU C++ reduction in operator.cpp. Its public C ABI is extern C void row_sum(const double* input, int rows, int cols, double* output). For integer dimensions 1 <= rows, cols <= 1024, input points to a contiguous row-major array of rows*cols finite IEEE 754 double values with absolute value at most 1e6, and output points to a separate writable array of at least rows doubles. Each output[row] must approximate the sum of that row's cols values. Allow ordinary double summation rounding, including cancellation: the absolute error relative to an accurately accumulated sum must not exceed 1e-12 + 2*cols*epsilon*sum(abs(row_values)), where epsilon=2^-52. Preserve the input and write exactly rows output elements; do not read other rows to compute a row's sum. Support rectangular arrays, one-column arrays, single rows, negative values, zero values, and fractional double values. Invalid pointers, overlapping input/output, values or dimensions outside the stated bounds, nonfinite values, overflow, and parallel or GPU execution are outside scope. Keep the function name and C ABI so ctypes can load it. Build the candidate from the source workspace using c++ -shared -fPIC -O2 operator.cpp -o liboperator.so, then run python3 test_public.py -v. The evaluator runs this build command after applying each candidate patch and before loading workspace/liboperator.so. The shared library is a generated build artifact and is ignored by Git; submit changes to source and rebuild locally when testing. The baseline incorrectly repeats the first row's sum for every output row.
